title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics and tool message formatting for function calling
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: align Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer with the evolving OpenAI function/tool calling semantics (tool_choice, schema mapping, and tool message formatting). This change makes the compat layer: 1) interpret and surface tool_choice decisions from models, 2) map OpenAI-style tool/schemas to Redwood internal tool definitions (name, input_schema, verbatim params mapping), and 3) emit a stable formatted tool message payload that the runtime and SDKs can consume for deterministic replay and observability. What this PR does: - Adds tool_choice parsing in the compat layer and a deterministic tie-break rule for 'tool variants' when model returns multiple choices. - Introduces a lightweight schema-mapping layer so OpenAI 'parameters' objects are validated and coerced into Redwood tool input shapes (basic type coercion and required-field checks). - Updates tool message formatting to consistently include metadata (tool_version, mapped_schema_id, origin: "openai_compat", and raw_model_choice) for downstream runtimes and audit logs. - Exposes a compact event in the trace pipeline when a tool_choice is accepted/overridden for observability. - Adds unit and integration tests that cover common edge cases (duplicate tool names, nested parameter coercion, missing required fields). Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4218) - [x] Tests added for parsing and mapping - [x] SDK plumbing updates (Python compat module) - [x] CI passing locally and on CI - [x] Backwards-compatible: does not change existing non-OpenAI flows. Related: linear ENG-4218, ENG-4240. See design notes in openai-compat/README and API contract in docs/openai_compat.md.

review_comments: Daniel Park: Overall looks good. Two asks: add explicit tie-break section in the code comments (how we pick between tool variants) and add a perf note for the extra validation step.
Ava Chen: Reply: added code comment + cheap pre-check that returns fast-fail for clearly invalid payloads. Perf note added to schema_mapper.rs.
Sofia Martinez: Please ensure SDK surface doesn't leak internal schema ids; prefer mapped_schema_id in payload but keep internal ids opaque to users.
Ava Chen: Reply: mapped_schema_id is a stable string token; SDK will expose only the token and not internal DB ids. Updated unit tests to assert opacity.
Priya Raman: Approve after tests. Observability event looks good but can we include the raw_model_choice in debug logs only?
Ava Chen: Reply: agreed; raw_model_choice is attached in trace/obs at debug level and still included in the tool message provenance field for audit (non-sensitive).
